project.name: rtunk
project.description: A from-scratch, fully open-source rewrite of trunk.io's Code Quality CLI: an orchestrator for linters, formatters, and security scanners behind a single declarative config, with hermetic per-project tool versions, git-aware changed-file checks, output normalization, and caching, built as an auditable, fully local alternative with no telemetry, cloud account, daemon, or self-upgrade.

tour.title: What rtunk Is
tour.description: README.md explains why rtunk exists: an open-source Go rewrite of the trunk.io Code Quality CLI that stays compatible with trunk configuration. AGENTS.md adds the vision and the rules contributors follow. Together they frame the problems the rest of the tour solves.

tour.title: Architecture Overview
tour.description: docs/Architecture.md gives the component map and domain model that the following steps walk through one by one. Read it as the table of contents for the code: CLI, config, plugins, cache, engine and output parsing.

tour.title: Binary Entry Point
tour.description: cmd/rtunk/main.go is deliberately thin: it resolves the build version from ldflags or module info and hands control to the CLI package. Everything of substance lives behind this call, which is where Step 4 picks up.
tour.languageLesson: Go binaries start in package main's main(). Keeping it tiny and pushing logic into internal/ packages keeps the code testable, since main itself cannot be imported.

tour.title: The CLI Command Tree
tour.description: internal/cli builds the command tree: cli.go wires the root, and check, fmt and the other command groups hang off it. shared.go holds helpers used across commands, and errors.go maps failures to exit codes. The commands are thin orchestration over the packages in the next steps.

tour.title: Trunk Configuration Model
tour.description: pkg/trunk/config is the most depended-on package. config.go declares the resolved Config, definitions.go the YAML plugin definitions (tools, linters, commands, actions, runtimes), and resolve.go loads trunk.yaml plus plugin sources. The ARCHITECTURE.md alongside it explains the two-layer config and plugin system that rtunk mirrors from trunk.
tour.languageLesson: YAML decoding in Go relies on struct tags (yaml:"name"). Declaring definitions as plain structs gives a typed, validated view of plugin files.

tour.title: Plugin Model and Sources
tour.description: These docs explain how plugin repositories, sources and the catalog fit together, and how local and remote sources are resolved in two layers. They are the conceptual background for the resolver you just saw in Step 5.

tour.title: Running Checks: The Engine
tour.description: check_run.go loads the config, selects files and drives the engine, which is where linting actually happens. pkg/run/engine builds a job per linter and file group, installs tools, runs commands and collects findings. match.go decides which files each linter sees, and configlink.go links config files into the run workspace.

tour.title: Normalizing Linter Output
tour.description: Every linter prints something different, so pkg/trunk/output converts each format (SARIF, ESLint, Pylint, regex-based and so on) into a single normalized Finding type. The engine from Step 7 depends on this package so that rendering and autofix can treat all linters uniformly.

tour.title: Cache and Tool Installation
tour.description: Linters need their tools, and pkg/cache/download fetches runtimes and tools into a single-root cache with locking, extraction, shims and pruning. Language-specific installers in pkg/cache/runtime (node, python, go and others) cover package-based tools. Cache-Architecture.md documents the layout and consistency rules.

tour.title: Formatting and Autofix
tour.description: fmt reuses the engine in formatter mode, skips partially staged files and can verify that repeated formatting is stable. The engine's autofix.go applies inline fixes from findings, converting UTF-16 offsets to byte offsets. This builds directly on the check flow from Step 7.

tour.title: Rendering Results
tour.description: The render package presents engine events as human-readable text, JSON, SARIF or an animated live TTY view, chosen by a factory in render.go. The base renderer collects events and dedupes findings so each format only handles presentation. Terminal-UX-Design.md explains the UX decisions.

tour.title: Actions, Hooks and Run Logs
tour.description: Actions run on triggers such as git hooks. pkg/run/actions resolves and executes them, and pkg/run/githooks installs rtunk-managed hooks. pkg/run/runlog records each run as JSONL events that logs show can replay.

tour.title: CI/CD and Releases
tour.description: The GitHub workflows test and lint on pull requests and the merge queue, run scheduled security scans, publish the wiki, and cut releases through a manually dispatched pipeline. As a capstone, this shows how the project ships what the previous steps describe.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows declare triggers under on:, parallel jobs, and sequential steps. Merge queue support needs the merge_group trigger.

tour.title: Contributing Next
tour.description: CONTRIBUTING.md covers the dev environment and tests, and ROADMAP.md shows what is planned next. Use them to pick a first change in any of the layers covered above.
